study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
cohort: 89 pregnant women with poorly controlled PGDM (HbA1c > 6% at 3 months prior to conception or during the first trimester) who gave birth between 2010 and 2019.
finding: While higher periconceptional HbA1c levels were associated with an increased risk of preterm delivery, there was no consistent association observed with other adverse pregnancy outcomes.
